seo.title: Your Life at Every Level of Getting Sued by a Debt Collector
seo.title_b: Sued Over a $3,812 Credit Card: Every Level, Letter to Paycheck
seo.hook: An envelope from a company you've never heard of says you owe $3,812. This is every level that follows in California, from the first letter to the day your paycheck shrinks.
seo.summary:
An old credit card you stopped paying in 2023 comes back as an envelope from a debt buyer you've never heard of. This video follows a made-up worker in California through every level of a debt collection lawsuit, in time order: the validation notice and the 30-day written dispute window (FDCPA / Regulation F), the 7-calls-in-7-days rule, California's debt collector license and the Rosenthal Act, the 4-year limit to sue on a written contract and the ban on suing over time-barred debt, the summons (SUM-100) and the 30 days to answer, what a debt buyer's complaint must list under California's Fair Debt Buying Practices Act (charge-off balance, interest and fees added after, every buyer, the contract attached), why debt buyers can't use small claims, the $225 answer fee and the FW-001 fee waiver, what Pew found about default judgments, the 6-month limit to set aside a default, 5% judgment interest on credit card judgments under $50,000, California's wage garnishment formula with the 2026 minimum wage ($16.90 x 48 = $811.20), the $2,325 automatic bank account protection from July 1, 2026, the 2-month protection for federal benefits like Social Security, how long a judgment lasts and when a collection account leaves a credit report, and what the FTC found debt buyers pay per dollar.

Everyone in this story is made up, and so are the story's dollar amounts (the $3,812 balance, the $674 add-on, court costs, pay, rent and savings). Copperleaf Bank, Meridian Receivables and Harborline Asset Recovery are fictional names. The rules, deadlines and statistics come from the sources listed below. Real cases depend on the facts, the court and the county.

Chapters: see the chapter list (Level 1: The letter ... Level 10: The long shadow, The end: What it cost).
seo.disclaimer: This video explains general California and federal rules for education and entertainment. It is not legal advice. Debt collection rules differ by state and change over time, and dollar amounts are adjusted regularly. If you have received a collection letter, a summons or a garnishment order, contact your court's self-help center, a legal aid office or a licensed attorney.

sources.title: 15 U.S.C. 1692g (FDCPA validation of debts: notice within 5 days; written dispute stops collection until verification)
12 CFR 1006.34 (Regulation F validation period: 30 days after receipt; receipt assumed 5 business days after sending)
12 CFR 1006.14(b)(2) (more than 7 calls in 7 days: rebuttable presumption of a violation)
12 CFR 1006.26(b) (no suit or threat of suit on time-barred debt)
DFPI – Debt Collection Licensing Act (Fin. Code 100000–100025; applications from Sept 1, 2021)
Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17 (Rosenthal Act incorporates FDCPA 1692b–1692j)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 337 (4 years on a written contract; no suit after the period runs)
Cal. Civ. Code 1788.56 (debt buyer may not sue after the statute of limitations)
Cal. Civ. Code 1788.58 (what a debt buyer's complaint must allege; contract attached)
Cal. Civ. Code 1788.60 (default judgment requires authenticated business records and the contract)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 412.20(a)(3) (30 days after service to respond)
California Courts Self-Help Guide – Respond to a debt lawsuit (Answer form PLD-C-010)
California Courts Self-Help Guide – Civil lawsuits (limited civil = $35,000 or less)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 116.420(a) (assignees can't file in small claims)
Judicial Council – Statewide Civil Fee Schedule effective Jan 1, 2026 (answer fee $225 limited up to $10,000)
California Courts Self-Help Guide – Fee waivers (FW-001)
California Courts Self-Help Guide – Default in a debt lawsuit (wait at least 30 days; CIV-100)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 473(b) (relief from default, no more than six months)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 685.010 (5% interest on personal debt judgments under $50,000, incl. credit cards)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 706.050 (wage garnishment: lesser of 20% or 40% above 48 x minimum wage)
California DIR news release 2025-118 (minimum wage $16.90 from Jan 1, 2026)
15 U.S.C. 1673 (federal garnishment cap 25%)
California Courts Self-Help Guide – Claim of exemption, wage garnishment (WG-006; creditor has 10 days to oppose)
Judicial Council report, June 29, 2026 (CCP 704.220 amount $2,244 to $2,325 from July 1, 2026)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 703.520 (claim of exemption: 15 days, 20 if served by mail)
31 CFR 212.6 and Appendix C (banks protect 2 months of direct-deposited federal benefits)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 683.020 / 683.110 (10 years; personal debt under $50,000 renewable once)
Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 697.310 (judgment lien on real property, 10 years)
15 U.S.C. 1681c (FCRA: collection accounts 7 years, from 180 days after delinquency began)
Pew Charitable Trusts (2020), How Debt Collectors Are Transforming the Business of State Courts
FTC press release, Jan 30, 2013 – debt buyers paid about 4 cents per dollar on average

Ny delstat (Kalifornien) och nytt rättsområde (skuldindrivning, utmätning) jämfört med Florida-krocken och Kalifornien-boten.

hooks_kandidater.A_vald: Mailbox 14B has never closed right. Tonight an envelope is sticking out of it. / It says you owe 3,812 dollars, and it gives you 30 days… (mekanism: specificity + stakes; bilden = miniatyren direkt; fungerar utan ljud tack vare $3,812 på brevet)
hooks_kandidater.B: The company suing you paid about 4 cents for every dollar it says you owe. (curiosity gap/dissonans – men första bilden blir ett kort, inte miniatyrens scen, och den största payoffen avslöjas direkt)
hooks_kandidater.C: Seven out of ten people sued over a debt never answer, and they lose without a hearing. (identitet/statistik – stark men abstrakt, ingen person i bild de första sekunderna)
hooks_kandidater.val: A – miniatyrens scen från bildruta 0, insats med siffra inom 5 s, löftet i klartext vid ~10 s; B:s gåta används som löfte vid ~22 s och betalas i slutet, C:s statistik kommer i nivå 6.

standard_check.krok: andra person från första meningen; plats + insats (lucka 14B, $3,812, 30 dagar) inom 10 s; löftet i klartext vid ~10 s ('from this envelope to your paycheck'); gåta (vem är Harborline? vad betalade de?) vid 16 och 28 s; första verkliga regeln (5 dagar, 1692g) vid ~33 s.
standard_check.nivåer: 10 nivåer + slut: The letter, The calls, The old card, The summons, The paper trail, The drawer, The default, The paycheck, The bank, The long shadow, What it cost; varje nivå: första ögonblick → det svåraste → verklig regel med källa (real-kort) → insidersanning → känsloslag → övergång.
standard_check.motiv: brevlåda 14B vars lock aldrig stänger (0:00, nivå 4, nivå 9, slutet när du lagar den) + kökslådan med hämtmatsmenyerna (nivå 1, 6, 7, 8, slutfrågan) + Dantes replik 'Paper beats phone' (nivå 2, 5, 8 – blir en verklig regel i nivå 2 och din egen replik i slutet).
standard_check.slut: cykeln: en ny granne i 14A står vid brevlådorna med ett kuvert från ett företag hon aldrig hört talas om; du säger Dantes replik; fäst fråga till tittaren om kuvertet i lådan.
standard_check.källor: 31 källor i beskrivningen (federal lag, CFR, Kaliforniens lagar, Judicial Council, domstolarnas självhjälpssidor, DFPI, DIR, Pew, FTC); källrad på varje real-kort.
standard_check.miljöer: mailroom (ny), apartment, loading_dock, collector_office, self_help_center (ny), court_hall, courtroom, bank – tom miljö först i nivå 7 (court_hall).
standard_check.tittartid: första 30 s: 4 helbildsscener med walk_to + 2 kort, ingen medium/närbild, ingen presentation de första 12 s, byte var ~5 s, slutlöfte vid ~10 s och ~25 s.

notes.påhittat: alla personer (du, Dante, Kyle, Inez, processdelgivaren, expediten, kommissionären, lånehandläggaren, den nya grannen), företagen Copperleaf Bank, Meridian Receivables och Harborline Asset Recovery, numret 916, alla belopp i berättelsen ($3,812, $3,400, $674, $4,486, $412 i rättegångskostnader, $4,898, $55, $400, $612,40, lön $1,050/v, $60/v efter förhandlingen, hyra $1,640, $2,610 på kontot, $340 sista betalningen), dagarna 9/35/52/60/70/82/90, 31 sidor, 28 timmar, 22 år, 11 minuter.
notes.uträkningar: $3,812 + $674 = $4,486; + $412 = $4,898; 48 × $16.90 = $811.20; $1,050 × 20 % = $210; ($1,050 − $811.20) × 40 % = $95.52 → lägst = $95.52; $4,898 / $95.52 ≈ 51 veckor ≈ 1 år; $4,898 / $60 ≈ 82 veckor ≈ 1,6 år; $2,610 − $2,325 = $285; 4 % × $3,812 = $152.48 ≈ $152; $4,898 / $152 ≈ 32 → 'more than thirty times'; dag 90 − dag 52 = 38; dispute window: brevet dag 1 + 5 arbetsdagar + 30 dagar ≈ dag 35+ (förenklat 'day 35'); preskription: sista betalning mars 2023 + 4 år = mars 2027 (förenklat – i praktiken räknas fristen från kontraktsbrottet/första missade betalningen); FCRA: försenad från ca april 2023 + 180 dagar + 7 år ≈ hösten 2030.
notes.osäkert: Kaliforniens lagtexter lästes på california.public.law/FindLaw (inofficiella speglar) eftersom leginfo gav fel – CCP 685.010 lästes på leginfo. 'Two years later … roughly 20 years at most' (683.110(c) förnyelse bara en gång) är förenklat. Lokala minimilöner högre än $16,90 gäller i vissa städer (706.050 använder den högre) – berättelsen anger ingen stad. 'Federal rules give her a shield … two months' – 31 CFR 212 gäller när banken får ett utmätningsbeslut och förmånen satts in direkt; vi säger 'when a garnishment order arrives'. Att kommissionären sänker beloppet till $60 är berättelse (domstolen KAN sänka). FTC:s 4 cent är ett genomsnitt från 2013 – videon säger 'if Harborline paid that average'. Pews siffror är från 2020 års rapport (data 1993–2013 och senare stickprov). Satisfaction of judgment: berättelse, ingen paragraf citeras.
